name: corner-response-quads-land-as-short-slices-of-a-runtime-region
rationale: The census's rwppCornerResponseShort writes its explicit imageblock of short4 cells to a texture2d<short> through a slice whose extent is [[threads_per_threadgroup]] << 1, a runtime value, at the ROI origin plus twice the threadgroup's first thread position; no authored case reached it. Each thread gathers nine 2x2 footprints of a half luma texture through a pixel-coordinate, clamp-to-edge constexpr sampler at (ROI + 2 gid + 1) and offsets 0, +-3 on each axis and +-2 diagonally, forms the Harris-like response dxx dyy - (dxy^2 + ((dxx + dyy) / 16)^2) in half, scales it by 1024 into a short, and stores (r, 0, 0, 0) in the four cells of its 2x2 quad; after the imageblock barrier thread (0, 0) writes the 8x8 block. The luma is 0 or 1 (a seeded random field with a solid 8x8 square and a cleared bar), so every half sum and product is exact (|r| <= 8 + 1/16 on a 1/256 grid, r * 1024 an integer within short) and fast-math reassociation cannot move a bit. The ROI (4, 4) with a 12x12 grid of 4x4 threadgroups keeps every gathered texel inside the 32x32 texture (1 to 30), so the answer depends on the footprints, not on the address mode. The output is RGBA16Sint (the slice's class comes from that format) poisoned with 0xAB: texels outside [4, 28)^2 keep the poison, which also states the block's origin and extent.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-five-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 25 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-four linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: round-to-half-from-65504-to-65520-and-past
rationale: Metal's rounding to half just past 65504, the largest finite half. STATUS wave 11 owes this reading (QuantizeToF16 65504..65520). D57.1 and D57.2 round every half result with OpQuantizeToF16, whose SPIR-V definition makes a value 'too large to represent' an infinity. Round to nearest even keeps every value below 65520 at 65504, and makes 65520 (a tie, 65504 being odd) and everything above it infinite. The answer decides the comparison class (D33) of every half result near the top of the range. The module is compiled -fno-fast-math, so the half fadd and fsub carry no ninf. Thread t = 0..4159 writes two words. Word 2t is half(x) | half(y) << 16, where x is the float of pattern 0x477fe000 + t (65504 + t/256: every float from 65504 through 65520 at t = 4096, then 63 past it) and y is its negation (pattern 0xc77fe000 + t, converted by its own fptrunc). Word 2t + 1 is (65504h + b) | (-65504h - b) << 16, for the half b of pattern 0x4000 + t: every half in [2, 34); the exact sum is 65520 at b = 16, t = 3072. Round to nearest even predicts 0x7bff (0xfbff) for x < 65520 and 0x7c00 (0xfc00) from 65520 on, and the same split for the sums at b = 16. A rounding that makes everything above 65504 infinite differs at t = 1..4095 and at b in [2, 16).

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-three-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 and 3 and receives exact float4 zero from both linked _uber_clear bodies. A five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected as the result. This entry writes the selected zero to both required poisoned output textures, with binding zero captured byte-exactly.

name: gpu-encoded-vertex-buffers-run-the-host-encoded-draws
rationale: A rasterization-disabled vertex function whose only effect is the render commands it encodes, observed only by executing them (DESIGN D249). The host encodes command 1's draw of 4 points from vertex 0 (one instance) and command 2's draw of 3 points from vertex 2 (2 instances from base instance 1); then the producer's point draw of 3 vertices reads the execution range (location 1, length 2), and vertices 0 and 1 each set command 1 + vid's vertex buffers 0 and 1 to the params and out windows at 256 * vid bytes and its fragment buffer 0 to params, keeping the host-encoded draw (vertex 2 is past the length and encodes nothing). The execution of commands 1 and 2 inherits the pipeline of the template (token 1, its own case) and no buffers: window 0's params are scale 3 and bias 5, so out words 0 to 3 hold 8, 11, 14, 17; window 1's are scale 7 and bias 11, and instance_id includes the base instance, so words 64 + 16 * iid + vid hold 7 * (vid + 1) + 11 + 1000 * iid: 1032, 1039, 1046 at words 82 to 84 and 2032, 2039, 2046 at words 98 to 100. Every other word keeps the 0xab fill, and every written byte differs from it.

name: neighbor-max-picks-the-middle-of-three-rows
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.convert.u.v2i16.s.v2i32 (28 case-less sources), the int2 -> ushort2 narrowing every one of this kernel three texture reads goes through. The source is one column of three texels and the compared output is the middle one, so the thread at gid (0,1) reads rows 2, 1 and 0 -- all in range -- and which texel it lands on is decided entirely by that conversion. The three z values are -4, -1 and -8, so the three-way argmax picks the middle row, and a conversion that lost the offset would pick a neighbour whose every component differs by at least a factor of sixteen. The selected texel is scaled by the half 0x3955 = 1365/2048; its 11-bit significand times a power of two is exact in binary16, so x, y and w are 1, 2 and 4 and the products are exact. Its z scales NEGATIVE, so the guarded reciprocal is not taken and the written z is a literal zero -- no half division has to be byte-authored. Expected texel is (0.66650390625, 1.3330078125, 0, 2.666015625). The threads at gid (0,0) and (0,2) read one row out of range and are deliberately outside the compared region.

name: a-kernel-encodes-the-stage-in-regions-of-its-dispatches
rationale: Kernel-encoded stage-in regions (DESIGN D336, D317 part 3c). Three producer threads each encode command t: the region of origin origins[t].xyz and size sizes[t].xyz, then a dispatch of origins[t].w threads in threadgroups of sizes[t].w: (2, 0, 0) size (6, 1, 1), 4 threads in one group; (9, 1, 2) size (5, 2, 1), 5 threads in one group; (16, 3, 4) size (16, 1, 3), 8 threads in two groups of 4. The commands inherit the pipeline, the template icb_stage_in_template (token 1, its own case: stage input 0 a uint of stride 4 stepping by thread position on x), and the buffers: out (3) at index 0 and the stage input's data (4, 32 uints, element i = 0x5000 + 3 * i) at index 1, the template's stage-input slot. Each command's threads lie in its region, so thread t of the command of origin o and size s writes out[o.x + t] = (0x5000 + 3 * (o.x + t), o.x | o.y << 8 | o.z << 16, s.x | s.y << 8 | s.z << 16, t): words 8 to 23, 36 to 55 and 64 to 95 (each uint4 four words). Every other word keeps the 0xab fill.

name: host-encoded-stage-in-regions-and-attribute-strides-of-executed-commands
rationale: Host-encoded stage-in regions and kernel-buffer attribute strides of compute commands (setStageInRegion:, setKernelBuffer:offset:attributeStride:atIndex:; DESIGN D327 item 5, D336). One command buffer of 3 commands supporting dynamic attribute strides (thread dispatches, 2 kernel buffers), inheriting the pipeline: the template icb_stage_in_template under a stage-input layout of MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic (token 1, its own case), so each fetch reads the stride its command binds the data with. The host binds every command's out (3) at index 0 and the stage input's data (4, 128 uints, element i = 0x5000 + 3 * i) at index 1 through the stride form: command 0 at stride 8, command 1 at stride 12, command 2 at stride 16. The host encodes command 1's region, origin (9, 1, 2) size (5, 2, 1), and 5 threads in one group, and command 2's, origin (24, 0, 0) size (8, 1, 1), and 8 threads in groups of 4. One producer thread encodes command 0's region, origin (2, 0, 0) size (6, 1, 1), and 4 threads in one group, over the host's bindings. Thread t of the command of origin o, size s and stride d writes out[o.x + t] = (the uint at byte d * (o.x + t) of the data, o.x | o.y << 8 | o.z << 16, s.x | s.y << 8 | s.z << 16, t): slots 2 to 5 read elements 2 to 5 at stride 8, slots 9 to 13 elements 9 to 13 at stride 12, and slots 24 to 31 elements 24 to 31 at stride 16. Every other word keeps the 0xab fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-four-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 24 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-three linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-three-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 23 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-two linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: fixed-point-bilinear-upscale-of-a-ushort-image
rationale: A 3x3 ushort image upscaled to 8x8 in fixed point. Every step is integer: the 16.16 step is (3<<16)/8, so the eight columns take fractions 0, 6, 12, 2, 8, 14, 4 and 10 out of 16 -- all four bilinear weights are non-trivial and different at nearly every texel, and the last column clamps its right neighbour back onto column 2. air.convert.u.v4i32.u.v4i16 widens each of the four gathered texels to 32 bits before the weighted sum, and air.convert.u.v4i16.u.v4i32 narrows the rounded result back. The four weights sum to exactly 256, so (sum + 128) >> 8 is an exact weighted average with no rounding freedom, and the largest intermediate is 65535*256 + 128, far inside u32. Source channels run to 65535 and to 0, so a narrowing that saturated instead of truncating, or one that widened with sign, would disagree on the very first texel.

name: half-conversion-by-gather-and-sampling-forms
rationale: How Metal converts texels to half in the sampling forms half-conversion-of-wider-texels-by-read-and-sample does not read. Four 16x16 half textures: rgba32_float values around half rounding boundaries (ties, ties plus or minus a few float ulps, the overflow edge, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, NaN, random), rgba16_unorm codes nearest a half tie with endpoints and random codes, and rgba8_unorm and rgba8_unorm_srgb with every code per channel. Lane i takes the pixel coordinate of texel (i mod 16, (i div 16) mod 16) at its centre (even i) or offset by seeded fractions k/256, k in 1..255 (odd i), divides it by the texture's size, and per texture writes seven results widened to float: gathers of components x and w and a nearest sample through a nearest clamp-to-edge sampler, and linear clamp-to-edge samples with constant offset (1, -1), level(0), bias(0.75), and zero gradients, to out[28i..28i+27] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: half-conversion-by-gather-and-sampling-forms-at-odd-sizes
rationale: How Metal converts texels to half in the sampling forms half-conversion-of-wider-texels-by-read-and-sample does not read. Four 13x11 half textures: rgba32_float values around half rounding boundaries (ties, ties plus or minus a few float ulps, the overflow edge, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, NaN, random), rgba16_unorm codes nearest a half tie with endpoints and random codes, and rgba8_unorm and rgba8_unorm_srgb with every code per channel. Lane i takes the pixel coordinate of texel (i mod 13, (i div 13) mod 11) at its centre (even i) or offset by seeded fractions k/256, k in 1..255 (odd i), divides it by the texture's size, and per texture writes seven results widened to float: gathers of components x and w and a nearest sample through a nearest clamp-to-edge sampler, and linear clamp-to-edge samples with constant offset (1, -1), level(0), bias(0.75), and zero gradients, to out[28i..28i+27] of buffer 1 in slot order, pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-zero-destination-lut-dequantize
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A single invocation computes coordinate zero while the authored destination extent is zero in every dimension. The top-level destination bounds guard returns before any source, LUT, destination, loop, or linked-function access, leaving the sole poisoned output unchanged. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: two-threads-four-steps-reduction-six-bounds-checked
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-destination case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents return at the top-level guard. kMPSUserConstant = 0x10400e4: identity dimension maps (every coordinate lane defined), dimensions y, z, w off, nResY 1, nSteps 4, 8-bit indices, quantization axis 0, no destination check, with the reduction bounds check; no per-threadgroup LUT. Two threads of one threadgroup walk reduction positions r = 4t while r < reductionSize 6 (the params' destination extents 8, 1, 1, 1 pass the z and w check), so thread 0 takes r = 0 and thread 1 r = 4. Each step reads its index through prefixPrimary_u8 (retained module returns 0), gathers the LUT at (0, 0, 0, 0) inside lut0Size (16, 1, 1, 1) through prefixSecondary_f (every retained module returns +0.0) and writes destination element r + s, s < 4, counting only steps whose index position is below 6, so thread 1 writes elements 4 and 5 and elements 6 and 7 keep the 0xab fill. Each written word is +0.0, written once by one thread; the reduction size and nSteps bound every loop.

name: two-threads-four-steps-reduction-six-unchecked-overhang
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-destination case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents return at the top-level guard. kMPSUserConstant = 0x400e4: identity dimension maps (every coordinate lane defined), dimensions y, z, w off, nResY 1, nSteps 4, 8-bit indices, quantization axis 0, no destination check, without the reduction bounds check; no per-threadgroup LUT. Two threads of one threadgroup walk reduction positions r = 4t while r < reductionSize 6 (the params' destination extents 8, 1, 1, 1 pass the z and w check), so thread 0 takes r = 0 and thread 1 r = 4. Each step reads its index through prefixPrimary_u8 (retained module returns 0), gathers the LUT at (0, 0, 0, 0) inside lut0Size (16, 1, 1, 1) through prefixSecondary_f (every retained module returns +0.0) and writes destination element r + s, s < 4, every step unchecked, so thread 1 also writes elements 6 and 7 past the reduction size. Each written word is +0.0, written once by one thread; the reduction size and nSteps bound every loop.

name: dsm-a-matrix-multiply-add-run-by-simdgroup-one-of-two
rationale: DESIGN D271 (a): a simdgroup multiply-add in a block the translator cannot prove workgroup uniform (the branch reads simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup), which only whole simdgroups execute at run time. One threadgroup of 64 threads: simdgroup 1 (threads 32-63) runs it, simdgroup 0 does not. Metal defines the multiply-add only on a whole simdgroup. Metal's answer is the product for threads 32-63 and the poison for 0-31. Inputs (A): a is the row rotation a[r][(r + 4) & 7] = 1 (else 0), b[k][j] = 8k + j + 1, c[r][j] = 256 + 8r + j, so a whole simdgroup's d[r][j] = b[(r + 4) & 7][j] + c[r][j]: each result row is the b row four rows away, which another half of the simdgroup holds. Every cell, product, and sum is an integer below 2048, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.

name: read-a-uniform-member-from-a-cloned-continuation
rationale: The structurizer CLONES blocks to give a nested selection a private merge, and it renames every value it duplicates. The emitter keys which buffer parameter is addressed as raw words by NAME, and derives that set before the CFG is structured, so the clone of an inlined helper's buffer parameter was missing from it -- and that membership is what carries the parameter's byte cursor. Every load through the cloned copy folded to OpConstantNull with spirv-val happy. The AIR here is hand-written because the CFG is the point: an inner selection inside an outer arm whose in-arm continuation the ENCLOSING arm also reaches, so that continuation is not dominated by the inner header and has to be privatized. The helper call lives in exactly that continuation, so the clone renames its inlined parameter. The .metal beside it spells the same answer without the CFG, which is all the Metal oracle needs. Buffer 0 holds a decoy Coef a = (1000, 2000, 3000, 4000) and the read one, b = (10, 20, 3, 40). Threads 2 and 3 take the inner arm that leaves before the continuation and write exactly 7. Threads 0 and 1 reach the continuation through the INNER arm and threads 4 through 7 reach it through the ENCLOSING one -- the two entries the clone separates -- and both write b.c2 + 0.5 = 3.5. Both values are exact binary32. A folded zero writes 0.5 on the six continuation lanes; the decoy member writes 3000.5; reading the wrong Coef field writes 10.5, 20.5 or 40.5.

name: gather-three-embedding-rows-across-a-short-last-threadgroup
rationale: A 10-thread dispatch in threadgroups of 4 is three threadgroups of 4, 4 and 2, so the last one is short and the exact-thread region plan has to run two regions: a full region of two groups and a tail region of one group whose threadgroup_base is 2. Each threadgroup copies one five-float embedding row, striding k from thread_position_in_threadgroup by threads_per_threadgroup, so the copy is complete only when threads_per_threadgroup is the SHORT groups actual two rather than the nominal four - at four, indices 2 and 3 of the last row are never written and keep the -7 poison. threadgroup_position_in_grid must also be 2 in the tail region, not 0, or the last row is gathered from the wrong weights row. The row selector is 2,0,1 so no row is copied to its own index, which makes a dropped or misordered gather visible rather than accidentally right. The fifteen output floats are pinned by hand.

name: linked-single-unit-tile-gradient
rationale: One invocation is admitted by unit destination bounds. Unit x, y, and z multiples make each nested reduction loop execute exactly once; the exact secondary prefix returns zero and the overwrite specialization selects the exact primary postfix, which writes zero to the sole poisoned device-buffer element.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: broadcast-one-depth-texel-into-a-float4-without-transposing-its-coordinate
rationale: A `depth2d<float, read>` fetch returns one scalar, and this case makes that scalar name its own texel. The 4x3 depth texture holds (y*4 + x + 1)/16, which is exact in binary32 for every texel and injective, and the coordinate buffer asks for (2, 1) -- so the answer must be 7/16 = 0.4375 and a transposed read would return 10/16 = 0.625 instead. The single returned float is splatted across all four lanes of a float4, so a fetch that filled only the red channel and left the rest undefined could not pass. The target buffer is 32 bytes while the store is a 16-byte float4 at offset 0, so its second half keeps the 0xCC poison and shows the store did not overrun.

name: fragment-depth-stencil
rationale: A generated full-coverage triangle executes the fragment entry against poisoned depth and stencil attachments; exact stencil byte 7 proves the separate depth/stencil output contract.
